Source history begins from the real upstream baseline and records the extension with concise meaningful commits. The README explains purpose, architecture, setup and test commands, and links to the real GitHub project. Local check success and server-enforced branch protection are recorded separately.
 
 ## 9. Supervised process and improvements
 
 The process began with course-document analysis and existing-source inspection. Requirements and acceptance examples were written before implementation. The initial approved slice connected evidence, review and a paper ledger so there was an early end-to-end workflow. This reduced integration uncertainty before adding the live experiment. The project then used measured failures and code review to choose the next changes.
 
 OpenCode's first session generated the application and tests. Its raw record includes implementation attempts, test failures and corrections. The coordinating review examined business contracts instead of relying entirely on the agent's success statement. The review caught the difference between a ticket cap and total holdings, the omission of shares from approval binding, and the unintended rejection of all sales. It also noticed that an empty-memory compaction example could pass while delivering no useful savings on the planned workload.
 
 The first session continued cleanup after its offline milestone. The coordinator ended that session and opened a shorter, focused live-evaluation session. This preserved the useful source changes and reduced the cost of repeatedly carrying a large context. The second prompt named the precise defects, fixed corpus, adapter behavior and required live commands. It did not ask the agent to revisit the entire project or produce another broad plan.
 
 Work was divided by ownership to avoid conflicting edits. The core OpenCode session handled application and tests. A separate OpenCode session handled CI scripts and schema. Documentation was maintained alongside the source, and a video workflow captured actual CLI commands in an isolated demo home. The remote repository work waited for a concrete local deliverable. This parallel structure used the API waiting time productively while keeping each code owner bounded.
 
 Defect trends are described from actual observations rather than invented issue counts. Early failures concerned packaging, context bookkeeping and a recovery transition. Later review findings concerned business semantics and experimental validity. That progression suggests the implementation became mechanically runnable before it fully represented the approved contracts. The improvement was to move from broad test counts to a smaller number of discriminating examples at each authority boundary.
 
 Ambiguity resolution is explicit. “No shorting” was interpreted as allowing a sell up to owned shares. “Ten percent position” constrains total holdings after a buy, while a valid sale can reduce an overweight holding. “Approval” covers quantity and material evidence. “Replay” reconstructs a saved result, while “rerun” regenerates one from fixed input. “Token reduction” refers to actual provider usage. These definitions are reflected in the requirements, ADRs and tests so later maintenance does not have to reconstruct the reasoning from a conversation.
 
 Artifacts co-evolved through the trace matrix. A change to the holdings interpretation affected the policy owner, approval decision, test examples and defect diary. A change to the context strategy affected ADR-001, the runtime adapter and evaluation method. Updating the JSON schema ensured that automated validation checked the committed requirements registry, while the AI-use gate verified that session logs stayed synchronized with source and prompt paths.
 
 The project also separates review authority from outcome evidence. A decision can authorize a plan, but it cannot declare an unrun test successful. An ADR can select an architecture, but it cannot establish measured token savings. A workflow file can define checks, but it cannot prove a server rejected a merge. This separation made the final deliverable more reviewable and prevented documentation from outrunning implementation.
 
 ## 10. Limitations and remaining risks
 
 The application is a local teaching research desk. Its approval identity is the local operator identifier and does not provide enterprise authentication. It does not connect to a broker or model real execution costs. Portfolio valuation uses the documented evidence/mark convention, and the workload does not establish multiuser concurrency guarantees. A network service would require a separate architecture decision for identity and transaction isolation.
 
 The six-case experiment evaluates context engineering on a defined frozen corpus. It does not establish investment profitability, general financial forecasting performance or robustness to every future market regime. Cases include actual prices and official releases, but the selected corpus is smaller than an unrestricted research environment. Independent live judgments remain model assessments and are preserved for inspection. Deterministic facts and policy results do not rely on those judgments. In the development MSFT compact report, the model divided the stock price by a single-quarter EPS and labeled the result a trailing P/E. The calculation used visible numbers, but the earnings-period interpretation was wrong. The judge still assigned support 0.9. This concrete failure shows why a passing research-quality threshold does not certify every financial interpretation. A valid citation rate of 1.0 refers only to the claims the judge counted as cited; it is not complete citation coverage or 100% factual accuracy. The raw judgments retain their uncited-claim and verification notes.
 
 The baseline tag was newly released and is supported here by the recorded regression run. Future upstream or provider changes can invalidate adapter assumptions and require another full test cycle. Offline replay establishes reconstruction of captured state, while a controlled live rerun can produce a different recommendation. The private GitHub account currently blocks Actions execution and branch-protection access. The repository and workflow files are published, while server execution and merge protection remain unavailable until the account limitations are resolved.
 
 The submission archives the complete native OpenCode transcripts alongside stage-mapped annotations, pairing all experimental and deployment records directly with their saved artifacts.
 
 ## 11. Individual reflections
 
 ### Alfa
 
 Requirements engineering on an agentic codebase succeeds or fails on how tightly natural-language rules constrain edge-case states. During the initial specification of the 23-item registry and MoSCoW priorities, prose descriptions of trading safety appeared unambiguous. Early implementation review revealed that short phrases hid divergent interpretations that passing unit tests did not immediately expose. A ten percent position limit initially passed verification when checked against a single order ticket of 100 shares at USD 100 in a USD 100000 account, yet that check failed to prevent a second purchase from pushing cumulative equity exposure above the cap. Similarly, a blanket prohibition on short selling was first realized in code as a total ban on sell orders, which blocked legitimate position reductions, and the initial approval fingerprint bound instrument symbol and evidence price while omitting operator-selected share quantity. Resolving these gaps required updating ADR-002 and linking each requirement to discriminating negative acceptance tests in AT-04 and AT-05. The held-out META compact run provided another requirements lesson when the report used the ticker and short name while omitting the full legal string Meta Platforms, Inc., leaving 59 of 60 checks passing under QUALITY-001 despite strong semantic scores. Separating Must invariants from Should performance targets established a stable decision framework before live metrics arrived, ensuring that a 45.73% token reduction could not excuse a missing identity field or relax a ledger rule. For future review practice, specification work will pair every numeric invariant with multi-step state-transition counterexamples before code generation starts. Requirements involving generated prose will separate deterministic format contracts, such as exact legal entity strings and evidence prices, from rubric-based semantic evaluation, ensuring that schema validators verify structural identity fields directly at the output boundary. The revised scope also makes five substantial increments visible across the team. Evidence portability and approved execution establish user-facing behavior. Context efficiency, bounded inputs and release-quality checks supply separate measurable engineering requirements. Keeping each increment attached to an owner and a fit criterion makes the contribution table useful during review, without treating document counts as a measure of engineering effort.
 
 ### Bravo
 
 Designing the extension seams and context budget around TradingAgents v0.4.0 highlighted the difference between a locally valid utility and a workload-effective architecture. Evaluating three architectural options led to wrapping the unmodified upstream graph with application-owned adapters rather than rewriting core agent nodes or substituting a toy pipeline. That choice preserved upstream analyst roles and structured state propagation while isolating context assembly and call accounting in dedicated modules. The first context compaction implementation demonstrated a classic architectural pitfall: the code deduplicated past reflection memory and passed isolated unit tests, yet fresh evaluation runs across the six equity cases began with almost no prior memory. Workload inspection showed that dominant token consumption came from repeated per-agent prompt history and verbose intermediate responses passing across the graph. Redirecting compaction to filter active message layers while re-injecting standing constraints, ticker identity, analysis cutoff, and task instructions at every request boundary made the optimization effective on actual runs and corrected the initial zero-citation failure recorded in prompt version research-desk-0.1.1. Request budgeting exposed a similar boundary issue, because checking a counter after a response arrives or relying on framework callbacks that swallow exceptions cannot stop an over-budget API call or a structured-output retry. Enforcing the budget check immediately prior to provider invocation allowed the max_calls=1 run to halt cleanly at 2273 tokens with a budget_stopped status while preserving diagnostic state. In future architecture reviews, component designs will be validated against empirical token and call profiles from a pilot trace prior to full implementation, and every resource cap or standing prompt constraint will be verified at the lowest-level provider adapter boundary rather than assumed to survive framework propagation. A further design distinction concerns call limits and input size. They bound different resources. A complete context cap must include tool responses and standing instructions, while compaction must preserve their logical relationships. The planned request-boundary revision therefore has explicit acceptance cases for oversized mandatory evidence and matching tool identifiers. This provides a concrete basis for evaluating the next architectural decision.
 
 ### Charlie
 
 Building the evidence capture pipeline and proposal state machine showed that deterministic authority depends on controlling every data path and transition edge around a stochastic model. Relying solely on standard LangChain model and tool callbacks initially left blind spots because upstream instrument resolution and return-history reads accessed data outside ordinary tool invocations. Subclassing the adapter to capture and freeze those direct reads closed the completeness gap so exported ZIP packages could replay in fresh processes with zero network calls in under 0.82 seconds. Real execution during the initial AAPL pilot exposed two boundary defects at export time: unserialized LangChain message objects in the terminal state broke JSON packaging, and an overly broad credential-redaction regex stripped numeric token usage fields alongside secret keys. Fixing serialization at the capture boundary and scoping redaction strictly to authentication strings preserved complete audit data without leaking credentials. On the transaction side, separating the Review module from Policy and SQLite Storage ensured that model text could never mutate the ledger, while cryptographic fingerprinting tied operator approval to the exact combination of evidence package, direction, price, and share quantity. State-machine testing also revealed that safety requires recoverability: when an unapproved or modified proposal entered REVIEW_REQUIRED, the earliest transition table locked the record instead of permitting the operator to inspect and approve the updated terms. Ongoing defect analysis further indicates that rejected proposals must preserve an explicit terminal status after an attempted execution. In future engineering reviews, state-machine verification will require a full transition matrix covering recovery and terminal rejection states, and serialization schemas will be tested against raw framework objects captured from live runs before final evaluation begins. The newly reproduced rejection path makes transition coverage especially important. Calling execute on a rejected proposal should preserve rejection, including when approval is attempted afterward. A test that invokes approve directly cannot establish that longer sequence. Small examples with an isolated store make the intended state change explicit and expose which module owns the correction. That distinction will guide subsequent code reviews.
 
 ### Delta
 
 Structuring the three-tier verification suite and executing the twelve-run evaluation matrix demonstrated that measurement pipelines require the same debugging rigor as application code. Offline verification progressed from 47 initial tests to 98 application tests alongside 649 passing upstream checks, using socket-blocked subprocesses and controlled fixtures to verify replay isolation and the ten percent equity cap. When evaluation moved to live DeepSeek runs across the two development cases and four held-out cases, two distinct failures emerged in the evaluation harness itself. First, the initial AAPL and MSFT runs achieved a 36.07% token savings but scored zero on citation validity because standing grounding rules did not reach downstream roles; archiving that failed batch under evaluation/development-initial and updating the request adapter resolved the defect before opening the held-out split. Second, during final scoring, the convenience input projection passed to the independent judge retained only the last tool output when an agent invoked the same tool name multiple times, hiding earlier observations that remained intact in the canonical event stream. Rebuilding the judge input from the complete recorded event stream and re-running all twelve judgments restored observation fidelity without altering any model output or rubric threshold, while keeping both sets of judge transcripts and their 241278 and 236462 token costs transparent. Even with a 0.9000 compact support mean, the MSFT compact report divided share price by single-quarter EPS to state a trailing P/E ratio while still receiving a 0.9 support score from the LLM judge. Future evaluation reviews will audit data projections against canonical event logs before invoking judge models and will pair LLM rubrics with deterministic domain checks for period alignment and financial formulas. Release evaluation also needs a link to the implementation being assessed. A successful archived score becomes stale when the prompt or evaluator changes. Binding each fresh run and its judgment to the evaluated source makes this relationship explicit. Unit cases for missing results and stale evidence can then verify the acceptance mechanism without consuming additional model calls or replacing a real experiment.
 
 ### Echo
 
 Managing continuous integration, packaging, and repository governance demonstrated that automated enforcement is only as reliable as the environment and schemas backing it. Early integration exposed a basic packaging flaw when the generated src-layout omitted package discovery settings in pyproject.toml, preventing the research-desk CLI from importing until the build configuration was repaired and tested in an isolated environment. Designing the six local verification gates required coupling documentation artifacts directly to executable validators across test chronology, static typing and linting, requirements schema compliance, offline semantic replay, full regression suites, and AI-use log synchronization. The initial unified gate run archived in evaluation/ci-initial proved the value of testing the validators themselves: static validation failed on an unresolvable external JSON Schema URI when run offline, and the AI-use gate missed a test directory marker. Fixing those defects and running six deliberate negative probes confirmed that the local pipeline rejected bad chronology, unapproved safety edits, and schema violations in the saved local execution. Release execution then highlighted the boundary between local reproducibility and hosted platform governance. Although the private GitHub repository received the verified commit history and signed upstream v0.4.0 tag, the initial remote GitHub Actions runs were blocked prior to job execution by account billing limits, and private repository branch protection returned HTTP 403 under the current plan. Recording the exact API responses and desired protection payload in evaluation/github preserved an honest audit trail for D7 and GOV-004. In future release workflows, repository hosting constraints, runners, and branch-protection permissions will be probed with an early actual workflow run at project initialization, and all schema validators will be forced to run under strict network isolation from day one. The current completion work has made the repository public with explicit authorization. A fresh hosted run has passed all six existing checks, and main now requires those checks plus a code-owner review. The remaining task is to carry the revised implementation through that same protected route. This turns the release plan into observable platform behavior and gives the final reviewer a concrete merge decision.
 
 ## 12. Reproducibility and deliverable map
 
 The complete D1–D9 path index is docs/deliverable-index.md. The repository contains the requirements registry and JSON schema under docs/req. Architecture artifacts include the root blueprint, ADRs, invariant register, trace matrix, memory design, permission model, runtime policy catalog and candidate evaluation. Governance files include AGENTS.md, Prompt.md, project rules, structural constraints and verification constraints. The review memo, debt register and defect diary preserve significant decisions and findings.
 
 Source is under src/research_desk and the original upstream directories remain intact. Deterministic tests are under test/offline. Frozen public inputs and recorded fixture packages are identified separately. Live evaluation artifacts contain per-case evidence and aggregated results. The transcripts directory preserves complete native OpenCode sessions, original event streams and annotations. Credential-only redaction is distinguished from optional broadly sanitized convenience exports. The final report is this single Markdown document, with a 12-point single-spaced PDF rendering supplied for page-count inspection. The 600-second MP4 demonstration is a separate deliverable and is not embedded in the source ZIP.
 
 A reviewer should first read the README and run the deterministic suite. The isolated demonstration then shows export, replay, approval, execution and rejection. The live experiment can be repeated with an explicitly provided DeepSeek key and the saved fixed inputs. Repetition may incur API charges and produce different reasoning; the archived original results remain the evidence for this report's numerical claims. The environment lock records the actual installed dependency versions without including local credentials or editable absolute paths.

 # Permission model
 
 The principle is no access until a role needs a path. The machine-readable permissions and effective OpenCode configuration must agree; a file named permissions.jsonc alone is not enforcement. The host keeps credentials outside agent-readable files and injects only the application's runtime environment.
 
 | Role | Read | Write | Forbidden |
 |---|---|---|---|
 | Plan | AGENTS, Prompt, docs, public upstream source, src/test declarations | proposed plan documents | Application implementation, approvals, secrets |
 | Build | Approved requirements/architecture/tests, src, test, pyproject | src/research_desk, approved test files, scoped package metadata | Human-owned rules/approval decisions, global config, upstream replacement |
 | Verify | Source, tests, requirements, frozen fixtures, run evidence | verification outputs and proposed test changes | Granting approval, weakening requirements, editing source to force a result |
-| Release | Final artifacts and local git state | package, workflow evidence, authorized private remote | Publishing credentials, public release, real orders |
+| Release | Final artifacts and local git state | package, workflow evidence, authorized project remote | Publishing credentials, real orders |
 | leo | All project decisions and review evidence | Plans, ADRs, rules, concrete stage approvals | Falsifying raw sessions or measured results |
 
 Runtime authority is separate from coding-agent permissions. The graph has market/news tools and model access. It has no review, execute or ledger tool. The local operator commands own approval and execution. This is a single-user workstation boundary, not a claim of production identity assurance.
 
 Safety-relevant paths include policy.py, review.py, storage.py, config.py, model contracts, permission configuration and rule files. Changes need a reviewed ADR plus a corresponding approval record. Current fixes to total holdings, valid sells and exact approval binding are covered by ADR-002 and the approved AT-04/05 semantics.
+
+
+The user authorized public repository visibility for this revision. The temporary revision role can modify only approved application/test/CI paths under ADR-004. It cannot edit governance or approval records and is removed after implementation.

 """Gate 5: full regression.
 
 Runs both the original upstream ``tests`` suite and the new ``test/offline``
-suite. Live API tests are excluded via the registered ``live`` marker. A silent
-pass or continue-on-error is not permitted: any non-zero exit fails the gate.
+suite. Tests marked ``integration``, ``live`` or ``smoke`` are excluded so CI
+makes no external-service or runtime model calls. A silent pass or
+continue-on-error is not permitted: any non-zero exit fails the gate.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import argparse
 from pathlib import Path
 
 from _gate_lib import add_change_args, fail, resolve_root, run, tool_path
 
 TARGETS = ("tests", "test/offline")
-EXCLUDE_MARKER = "live"
+EXCLUDE_MARKERS = ("integration", "live", "smoke")
+MARKER_EXPRESSION = " and ".join(f"not {marker}" for marker in EXCLUDE_MARKERS)
 
 
 def main() -> None:
     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Gate 5: full regression.")
     add_change_args(parser)
     args = parser.parse_args()
 
     root: Path = resolve_root(args.root)
     checks: list[str] = []
     failures: list[str] = []
 
     py = tool_path(root, "python") or "python"
     for target in TARGETS:
-        cmd = [py, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-m", f"not {EXCLUDE_MARKER}", target]
+        cmd = [py, "-m", "pytest", "-q", "-m", MARKER_EXPRESSION, target]
         proc = run(cmd, root)
         tail = "\n".join((proc.stdout or "").splitlines()[-6:])
         summary = _summary_line(proc.stdout)
         checks.append(f"pytest {target} -> exit {proc.returncode} ({summary})")
         if proc.returncode != 0:
             failures.append(f"regression suite failed: {target}")
             failures.append(f"  command: {' '.join(cmd)}")
             failures.append(f"  stderr tail:\n{(proc.stderr or '').strip()}")
             failures.append(f"  stdout tail:\n{tail}")
 
     fail(checks, failures)
 
 
 def _summary_line(stdout: str) -> str:
     """Extract the pytest totals line (e.g. '49 passed in 0.77s') from output."""
     for line in reversed((stdout or "").splitlines()):
         stripped = line.strip()
         if stripped and ("passed" in stripped or "failed" in stripped):
             return stripped
     return "no summary line"
 
 
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     main()

 """Per-agent COMMON grounding + prompt compaction on the real LLM inputs.
 
 Fresh evaluation runs have essentially no past memory, so compressing only
 ``past_context`` has almost no effect, and that header is not even read by many
 downstream upstream roles. This module fixes the shared grounding/citation
 failure by wrapping the real LangChain chat model with a small plain delegate
 (exposing ``invoke``, ``bind_tools`` and ``with_structured_output``) that
 injects the identical COMMON grounding layer into *every* request in BOTH modes
 (baseline and compact), while retaining the real LangChain client and the
 upstream ``GraphSetup``.
 
 - The common grounding layer carries the real per-case ticker, legal company
   identity, analysis date, frozen close, the source-ID registry
   (``src-<ticker>`` = official earnings news, ``market-<ticker>`` = market
   CSV/technical computations), the short official earnings notes and citation
   rules. It is the shared correctness fix applied to both arms.
 - For ``context_mode == "baseline"`` the delegate only prepends the common
   grounding layer; the substantive prompt/history is left uncompressed (no
   artificial padding, no rewrite).
 - For ``compact`` the delegate additionally trims redundant message text,
   de-duplicates, and appends a concise-output instruction, while preserving key
   quoted facts (the standing-constraints and source markers) in every prompt.
 
 Message integrity rules (review finding #1):
 
 - A message is rebuilt with the declared model-copy/update API, changing only
   ``content``. ``AIMessage.tool_calls``, ``ToolMessage.tool_call_id``,
   ``id``/``name`` and every other field are preserved — never re-created.
 - A ``ToolMessage`` that answers an assistant tool call is never de-duplicated
   away and never truncated: dropping or merging it would break the assistant's
   pending tool call.
 - An ``AIMessage`` that carries ``tool_calls`` (typically with empty ``content``)
   is kept, never dropped, even though its text is empty.
 - Evidence messages (messages carrying a ``_FACT_MARKERS`` token) are not
   truncated. Trimming only verbose, non-fact prose is allowed; discarding
   numbers, identity, dates or sources is not.
 - The concise-output instruction targets ~600 tokens for compact roles while
   the provider ``max_tokens`` stays 1800 in both arms (set in the graph config).
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import logging
-from typing import Any
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from typing import Any, TypedDict
 
 from langchain_core.messages import AIMessage, BaseMessage, HumanMessage, SystemMessage, ToolMessage
 
 from ..budget import ContextBudgetExceeded, estimate_input_units
 from ..config import DEFAULT_CONTEXT_MAX_TOKENS, DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TRIGGER_TOKENS
 
 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
 
+
+class BudgetObservation(TypedDict):
+    """Conservative whole-input budget observation emitted per request."""
+
+    before_units: int
+    after_units: int
+    trigger: int
+    cap: int
+    compacted: bool
+    metric: str
+
+
+BudgetObserver = Callable[[BudgetObservation], None]
+
 # Content markers that carry the facts which must survive compaction. A message
 # containing any marker is kept (not trimmed below the fact floor).
 _FACT_MARKERS = (
     "STANDING ANALYSIS CONSTRAINTS",
     "last_close",
     "NO_DATA_AVAILABLE",
     "source_id",
     "src-",
     "USD",
     "% of equity",
     "integer_shares",
     "no_shorting",
     "Analysis date",
     "Company:",
     "Instrument identity",
     "trade_date",
     "past_context",
 )
 
 # Concise-output target for the compact arm (~600 tokens) while the provider
 # ``max_tokens`` cap stays 1800 in both arms.
 _OUTPUT_INSTRUCTION = (
     "Respond concisely: keep your entire answer within {max_tokens} tokens. "
     "Do not repeat the input; only output the requested analysis."
 )
 
 
 def _tuple_to_message(role: str, content: Any) -> BaseMessage | None:
     """Map a ``(role, content)`` pair to a message, or None for an unknown role."""
     role = (role or "").lower()
     if role == "system":
         return SystemMessage(content=content)
     if role in ("human", "user"):
         return HumanMessage(content=content)
     if role in ("ai", "assistant"):
         return AIMessage(content=content)
     return None
 
 
 def _to_messages(input: Any) -> list[BaseMessage] | None:
     """Normalise a model input to a list of messages, or None if not list-like."""
     if isinstance(input, list) and all(isinstance(m, BaseMessage) for m in input):
         return list(input)
     if isinstance(input, str):
         return [HumanMessage(content=input)]
     if isinstance(input, (list, tuple)) and input and all(
         isinstance(p, (list, tuple)) and len(p) == 2 for p in input
     ):
         mapped = [_tuple_to_message(role, content) for role, content in input]
         if all(m is not None for m in mapped):
             return [m for m in mapped if m is not None]
         return None  # unknown role: pass through unchanged rather than drop content
     if hasattr(input, "to_messages"):
         try:
             return input.to_messages()
         except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - PromptValue edge cases
             return None
     return None
 
 
 def _content_of(msg: BaseMessage) -> str:
     c = msg.content
     return c if isinstance(c, str) else str(c)
 
 
 def _has_fact_marker(text: str) -> bool:
     low = text.lower()
     return any(marker.lower() in low for marker in _FACT_MARKERS)
 
 
 def _rebuild(msg: BaseMessage, content: str) -> BaseMessage:
     """Rebuild a message with only ``content`` changed; preserve every other field.
 
     ``model_copy(update=...)`` keeps ``type``, ``id``, ``name``, ``tool_calls``,
     ``tool_call_id``, ``additional_kwargs`` and any subclass state intact, so an
     ``AIMessage`` keeps its tool calls and a ``ToolMessage`` keeps the
     ``tool_call_id`` the assistant is waiting on.
     """
     return msg.model_copy(update={"content": content})
 
 
 def compact_transform(
     input: Any,
     *,
     max_output_tokens: int = 600,
     max_msg_chars: int = 1500,
     fact_floor_chars: int = 6000,
 ) -> Any:
     """Transform a per-agent prompt for the compact arm.
 
     Keeps message roles, trims verbose non-fact prose to ``max_msg_chars``,
     removes exact duplicate messages (never a tool response), and appends a
     concise-output instruction. Messages carrying key facts are preserved so no
     grounding marker is dropped. Every message is rebuilt via
     :func:`_rebuild`, so tool-call state survives unchanged.
     """
     messages = _to_messages(input)
     if messages is None:
         return input  # cannot transform; pass through unchanged
 
     seen: set[str] = set()
     kept: list[BaseMessage] = []
     for msg in messages:
         content = _content_of(msg)
         if isinstance(msg, ToolMessage):
             # A tool response answers an assistant tool call: never dedupe,
             # never truncate, never drop — the assistant is waiting on it.
             kept.append(msg)
             continue
         if isinstance(msg, AIMessage) and getattr(msg, "tool_calls", None):
             # An assistant message that issued tool calls (text may be empty);
             # keep it whole so the tool_calls survive to the next turn.
             kept.append(_rebuild(msg, content))
             continue
         if not content:
             continue
         if content in seen:
             continue  # drop exact duplicate prose messages only
         seen.add(content)
         if not _has_fact_marker(content) and len(content) > max_msg_chars:
             content = content[:max_msg_chars].rstrip() + "\n[... compacted ...]"
         kept.append(_rebuild(msg, content))
 
     kept.append(
         SystemMessage(content=_OUTPUT_INSTRUCTION.format(max_tokens=max_output_tokens))
     )
     return kept
 
 
 _COMPACTED_MARKER = "\n[... context compacted ...]"
 _BUDGET_PROSE_CHARS = 240
 
 
 def _is_expendable_old_prose(
     msg: BaseMessage, index: int, latest_human: int
 ) -> bool:
     """Whether an old, non-fact plain prose message may be compacted/removed.
 
     System constraints, the latest user/task, fact-bearing evidence and every
     assistant/tool-call group member are never expendable.
     """
     if index == latest_human:
         return False
     if not isinstance(msg, (HumanMessage, AIMessage)):
         return False
     if isinstance(msg, AIMessage) and getattr(msg, "tool_calls", None):
         return False
     if _has_fact_marker(_content_of(msg)):
         return False
     return True
 
 
 def enforce_context_budget(
     messages: list[BaseMessage],
     *,
     trigger_tokens: int,
     max_tokens: int,
     prose_chars: int = _BUDGET_PROSE_CHARS,
 ) -> tuple[list[BaseMessage], bool, int]:
     """Bound a complete message list, preserving mandatory material.
 
     Below ``trigger_tokens`` the input is returned unchanged. Above it, older
     expendable non-fact prose is first shortened and then dropped oldest-first.
     System constraints, the latest user/task, fact-bearing evidence and entire
     assistant tool-call / ToolMessage groups are never removed. If the required
     material still exceeds ``max_tokens``, raise :class:`ContextBudgetExceeded`
     before the provider is invoked.
 
     Returns ``(messages, compacted, before_units)``.
     """
     before = estimate_input_units(messages)
     if before <= trigger_tokens and before <= max_tokens:
         return list(messages), False, before
 
     latest_human = max(
         (i for i, m in enumerate(messages) if isinstance(m, HumanMessage)),
         default=-1,
     )
     expendable = [
         i
         for i, m in enumerate(messages)
         if _is_expendable_old_prose(m, i, latest_human)
     ]
 
     compacted_messages: list[BaseMessage] = []
     for i, msg in enumerate(messages):
         if i in expendable:
             content = _content_of(msg)
             if len(content) > prose_chars:
                 content = content[:prose_chars].rstrip() + _COMPACTED_MARKER
             compacted_messages.append(_rebuild(msg, content))
         else:
             compacted_messages.append(msg)
 
     after = estimate_input_units(compacted_messages)
     if after > max_tokens:
         dropped: set[int] = set()
         for i in expendable:
             dropped.add(i)
             candidate = [m for j, m in enumerate(compacted_messages) if j not in dropped]
             after = estimate_input_units(candidate)
             if after <= max_tokens:
                 compacted_messages = candidate
                 break
         else:
             compacted_messages = [
                 m for j, m in enumerate(compacted_messages) if j not in dropped
             ]
             after = estimate_input_units(compacted_messages)
 
     if after > max_tokens:
         raise ContextBudgetExceeded(after, max_tokens)
     return compacted_messages, True, before

 # A monetary number token in ordinary report formatting: optional ``$``/spaces,
 # an explicit sign, US thousands separators, and a decimal fraction. Ungrouped
 # integers of any length match, correctly grouped comma amounts match, and the
 # sign stays part of the numeric value so ``-451.10`` is never read as
 # ``451.10``. The boundaries reject a digit/comma/dot directly before and a
 # digit directly after, so the match is never a substring of a larger number
 # like ``1451.10`` for an expected ``451.10``.
 _PRICE_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(
     r"(?<![\d.,])\$?\s*[+-]?\s*(?:\d{1,3}(?:,\d{3})+(?:\.\d+)?|\d+(?:\.\d+)?)(?!\d)"
 )
 
 
 def _normalize_number_token(token: str) -> Decimal | None:
     """Parse a matched number token (``$``/commas removed, sign kept) into a Decimal."""
     cleaned = token.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip()
     try:
         return Decimal(cleaned)
     except InvalidOperation:
         return None

     """True when ``text`` states the expected close as its own number token.
 
     Ordinary formatting is normalized ($451.10, 451.1, comma thousands, trailing
     zeros), so the check accepts exactly the expected numerical value and never
     a different number or a substring of a larger number.
     """
     expected = Decimal(f"{expected_close:.2f}")
     for match in _PRICE_TOKEN_RE.finditer(text):
         value = _normalize_number_token(match.group(0))
         if value is not None and value == expected:
             return True
     return False

 def _judge_prompt(
     case: dict,
     report_text: str,
     deterministic: list[dict],
     available_sources: dict[str, Any],
     events,

     """Build the judge prompt from the *actual* frozen evidence captured in this pack.
 
     Supplies the official earnings notes, the fixed ticker/date/identity and
     source IDs, plus the real market evidence (market CSV, verified snapshot and
     official news) and every observed tool result recorded in the event log — so
     the judge can validate technical/history claims in the report. No
     baseline/compact identity is revealed.

         for c in deterministic

 - company: {identity.get('company_name', '')}
 - analysis date: {case['analysis_date']}
 - source_id: {case.get('source_id', 'n/a')}
 - official source URL: {case.get('source_url', 'n/a')}
 
 Official earnings notes (frozen source):
 {notes}
 
 Frozen latest close (from the actual market CSV): {case['latest_close']:.2f}
 
 Market evidence captured in this pack (actual frozen market data this run had available):
 {market_evidence or '(none present)'}
 
 Verified market snapshot captured in this pack:
 {verified or '(none present)'}
 
 Company news captured in this pack (official source):
 {news or '(none present)'}
 
 Observed tool outputs this report's run actually retrieved:
 {observed or '(none present)'}
 
 Deterministic checks already computed against the report:
 {facts}
 
 Judge the report below. Score support and relevance on 0-1 using the rubric:
 - support 1.0 = every key conclusion has direct support from the evidence; 0.8 = main conclusions supported with no key fabrication; 0.5 = important evidence gaps; 0 = key factual fabrication.
 - relevance 1.0 = fully focused on the requested ticker/date/task; 0.8 = core complete with minor redundancy; 0.5 = missing key parts; 0 = off task.

 def _valid_citation_rate(cited: int, supported: int) -> float | None:
     """Supported-cited fraction; a zero denominator is NOT an automatic pass."""
     if cited <= 0:
         return None
     return round(supported / cited, 4)

     """Structured judge output, including the dedicated semantic validity gate.
 
     ``semantic_valid`` defaults to ``False`` when a legacy or incomplete judge
     response omits it, so absence can never be read as a pass. Any recorded
     semantic error also forces it to ``False`` regardless of citation counts.
     """
 
     support: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
     relevance: float = Field(..., ge=0, le=1)
     cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
     supported_cited_claim_count: int = Field(..., ge=0)
     invalid_citation_explanations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
     uncited_factual_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
     semantic_valid: bool = Field(
         default=False,
         description=(
             "True only when earnings periods/units are correct and no key numerical "
             "valuation assertion is unsupported by the evidence."
         ),
     )
     semantic_errors: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
     rationale: str = ""

         if self.supported_cited_claim_count > self.cited_claim_count:
             raise ValueError(
                 "supported_cited_claim_count cannot exceed cited_claim_count"
             )
         return self
 
     @model_validator(mode="after")
     def _semantic_errors_invalidate(self):
         if self.semantic_errors:
             self.semantic_valid = False
         return self

 def run_aggregate(root: str | Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
     """Compute six paired baseline/compact metrics from existing run dirs.
 
     No model is called. Completed arms are included; a missing or non-completed
     arm is recorded as such. Judge scores, when present, are attached separately.
     """
     root = Path(root)
     cases = [c for c in (root.iterdir() if root.exists() else []) if c.is_dir()]
     paired: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
     for case_dir in sorted(cases):
         ticker = case_dir.name
         arms = {}
         for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
             summary = case_dir / mode / "summary.json"
             if not summary.exists():
                 arms[mode] = {"present": False}
                 continue
             data = json.loads(summary.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
             data["present"] = True
             judge_file = root / "judge" / ticker / mode / "judge.json"
             if judge_file.exists():
                 data["judge"] = json.loads(judge_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
             arms[mode] = data
         if not arms.get("baseline", {}).get("present") and not arms.get("compact", {}).get("present"):
             continue
         paired.append({"ticker": ticker, "baseline": arms.get("baseline"), "compact": arms.get("compact")})
     report = _aggregate_report(paired)
     _dump_json(root / "aggregate" / "summary.json", {"paired": paired})
     (root / "aggregate" / "report.md").write_text(report, encoding="utf-8")
     return {"paired": paired, "report": report}
 
 
 def _arm_value(arm: dict | None, key: str, default=None):
     if arm is None or not arm.get("present"):
         return default
     return arm.get(key, default)
 
 
 def _aggregate_report(paired: list[dict]) -> str:
     lines = [
         "# Baseline / Compact Aggregate (six paired metrics)",
         "",
         "Read from existing run outputs; no model calls. Judge scores are attached when present.",
         "",
         "| ticker | metric | baseline | compact | delta |",
         "|---|---|---|---|---|",
     ]
     metrics = [
         ("calls", "{:.0f}"),
         ("input_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("output_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("total_tokens", "{:.0f}"),
         ("wall_seconds", "{:.1f}"),
         ("outcome", "{!s}"),
     ]
     for p in paired:
         t = p["ticker"]
         for key, fmt in metrics:
             b = _arm_value(p.get("baseline"), key)
             c = _arm_value(p.get("compact"), key)
             b_s = "n/a" if b is None else fmt.format(b)
             c_s = "n/a" if c is None else fmt.format(c)
             delta = "—"
             if isinstance(b, (int, float)) and isinstance(c, (int, float)):
                 delta = _pct(b, c)
             lines.append(f"| {t} | {key} | {b_s} | {c_s} | {delta} |")
     for p in paired:
         for mode in ("baseline", "compact"):
             judge = _arm_value(p.get(mode), "judge")
             if isinstance(judge, dict) and not judge.get("error") and judge.get("support") is not None:
                 lines.append(
                     f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge support | {judge['support']:.2f} | — | — |"
                 )
                 lines.append(
                     f"| {p['ticker']} | {mode} judge relevance | {judge['relevance']:.2f} | — | — |"
                 )
     return "\n".join(lines)
 
 
 def _pct(b: float, c: float) -> str:
     if b == 0:
         return "—"
     return f"{(c - b) / b * 100:+.1f}%"

 """Deterministic teaching-policy engine for the simulated ledger.
 
-The policy is decided by leo (the simulated student), never by an LLM. Every
-check returns a plain list of human-readable results; the review layer turns a
-non-empty list of failures into a business rejection and leaves the ledger
-untouched (INV-002). Boundary behaviour is explicit: a position value exactly
-equal to 10% of equity is allowed (<=), one share more is rejected.
+The deterministic policy constants are defined in ``research_desk.config``;
+policy is never decided by an LLM. Every check returns a plain list of
+human-readable results; the review layer turns a non-empty list of failures into
+a business rejection and leaves the ledger untouched (INV-002). Boundary
+behaviour is explicit: a position value exactly equal to 10% of equity is
+allowed (<=), one share more is rejected.
 """
 
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from dataclasses import dataclass
 
 from .config import INITIAL_CASH, MAX_POSITION_PCT, NO_SHORTING
 from .models import LedgerState
 
 
 @dataclass
 class PolicyVerdict:
     allowed: bool
     checks: list[dict]  # each: {"check": str, "passed": bool, "detail": str}
     equity: float | None = None
     position_value: float | None = None
     cash_after: float | None = None
     shares_after: int | None = None
 
 
 def _owned_shares(ledger: LedgerState, ticker: str) -> int:
     pos = ledger.positions.get(ticker.upper())
     return pos.shares if pos is not None else 0
 
 
 def _revalue_equity(ledger: LedgerState, ticker: str, mark_price: float) -> float:
     """Equity with the target ticker's holdings re-marked at the evidence price.
 
     The position cap is expressed as a fraction of equity, so the equity base
     must mark the ticker under review at the same (frozen evidence) price used
     for the trade. Other positions keep their recorded average mark, which is
     made explicit in the check detail rather than silently revalued.
     """
     ticker = ticker.upper()
     total = ledger.cash
     for t, pos in ledger.positions.items():
         if t == ticker and mark_price is not None and mark_price > 0:
             total += pos.shares * mark_price
         else:
             total += pos.shares * (pos.avg_price or 0.0)
     return total
 
 
 class PolicyViolation(Exception):
     def __init__(self, reasons: list[str]):
         self.reasons = reasons
         super().__init__("; ".join(reasons))
 
 
 def evaluate_buy(
     ledger: LedgerState,
     ticker: str,
     shares: int,
     price: float,
     *,
     initial_cash: float = INITIAL_CASH,
     max_position_pct: float = MAX_POSITION_PCT,
 ) -> PolicyVerdict:
     """Evaluate a buy proposal against the current ledger.
 
     Rules (v1 teaching policy):
     1. shares must be a positive integer.
     2. price must be positive and present (it always comes from evidence).
     3. cost (shares * price) must not exceed available cash.
     4. after the buy, the *total* position in this ticker (existing holdings at
        the evidence price plus the new shares) must be <= 10% of equity.
     5. no shorting (buys only increase a long position; never negative).
 
     ``initial_cash`` is recorded for the ledger seed; the effective cash check
     uses the current ledger's cash, which is ``initial_cash`` plus the sum of
     prior cash deltas. The position cap is against *total holdings after the
     purchase*, re-marking this ticker's existing shares at ``price``.
     """
     ticker = ticker.upper()
     checks: list[dict] = []
 
     def check(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str) -> None:
         checks.append({"check": name, "passed": passed, "detail": detail})
 
     if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:
         check("integer_positive_shares", False, f"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}")
         return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)
 
     if price is None or not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or price <= 0:
         check("price_from_evidence", False, f"price must be a positive number from evidence, got {price!r}")
         return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)
 
     equity = _revalue_equity(ledger, ticker, price)
     owned = _owned_shares(ledger, ticker)
     shares_after = owned + shares
     position_value = shares_after * price
     cash_after = ledger.cash - shares * price
 
     check("cash_sufficient", cash_after >= -1e-9, f"cost={shares * price:.2f}, cash={ledger.cash:.2f}")
 
     cap_value = max_position_pct * equity
     check(
         "position_cap_10pct",
         position_value <= cap_value + 1e-9,
         f"total holdings after buy ({owned} existing + {shares} new = {shares_after} sh "
         f"@ {price:.2f} = {position_value:.2f}) <= {max_position_pct:.0%} * equity={cap_value:.2f}",
     )
 
     check("no_shorting", NO_SHORTING, "v1 policy is buy-only; sell proposals use evaluate_sell")
 
     return PolicyVerdict(
         allowed=all(c["passed"] for c in checks),
         checks=checks,
         equity=equity,
         position_value=position_value,
         cash_after=cash_after,
         shares_after=shares_after,
     )
 
 
 def evaluate_sell(
     ledger: LedgerState,
     ticker: str,
     shares: int,
     price: float,
     *,
     max_position_pct: float = MAX_POSITION_PCT,
 ) -> PolicyVerdict:
     """Evaluate a sell proposal against the current ledger.
 
     Sells are allowed only up to the shares actually owned (no shorting means
     a position can never go negative). The 10% concentration cap applies after a
     BUY; a valid SELL that reduces an owned position is permitted even if price
     appreciation means the remaining holding still exceeds 10% of equity.
     ``price`` comes from evidence; cash increases by ``shares * price``.
     """
     ticker = ticker.upper()
     checks: list[dict] = []
 
     def check(name: str, passed: bool, detail: str) -> None:
         checks.append({"check": name, "passed": passed, "detail": detail})
 
     if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:
         check("integer_positive_shares", False, f"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}")
         return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)
 
     if price is None or not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or price <= 0:
         check("price_from_evidence", False, f"price must be a positive number from evidence, got {price!r}")
         return PolicyVerdict(False, checks)
 
     owned = _owned_shares(ledger, ticker)
     equity = _revalue_equity(ledger, ticker, price)
     shares_after = owned - shares
     position_value = shares_after * price
     cash_after = ledger.cash + shares * price
 
     check(
         "sell_not_exceeding_owned",
         shares_after >= 0,
         f"cannot sell {shares} sh when {owned} sh are owned (no shorting); "
         f"sell at most {owned} sh",
     )
 
     return PolicyVerdict(
         allowed=all(c["passed"] for c in checks),
         checks=checks,
         equity=equity,
         position_value=position_value,
         cash_after=cash_after,
         shares_after=shares_after,
     )
 
 
 def raise_for_violations(verdict: PolicyVerdict) -> None:
     """Raise a PolicyViolation listing every failed check (no partial writes)."""
     if not verdict.allowed:
         reasons = [f"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}" for c in verdict.checks if not c["passed"]]
         raise PolicyViolation(reasons)
 
 
 def reject_reasons(verdict: PolicyVerdict) -> list[str]:
     return [f"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}" for c in verdict.checks if not c["passed"]]
 
 
 def policy_bounds(
     ledger: LedgerState,
     ticker: str,
     price: float | None,
     *,
     max_position_pct: float = MAX_POSITION_PCT,
 ) -> dict:
     """Deterministic policy limits for a proposal price against a ledger.
 
     Reported by offline replay so the *policy output* (the largest integer
     share count the teaching policy would allow) is reproduced without needing
     the operator's eventual share choice. ``max_by_cap`` is the additional
     shares a *buy* may add given existing holdings must stay within the total
     position cap.
     """
     if price is None or price <= 0:
         return {
             "price_present": False,
             "max_by_cap": None,
             "max_by_cash": None,
             "owned": _owned_shares(ledger, ticker),
             "equity": ledger.equity,
             "cash": ledger.cash,
         }
     cap_value = max_position_pct * _revalue_equity(ledger, ticker, price)
     owned = _owned_shares(ledger, ticker)
     max_total = int(cap_value // price)
     return {
         "price_present": True,
         "max_by_cap": max_total - owned,  # additional shares still within total cap
         "max_by_cash": int(ledger.cash // price),
         "owned": owned,
         "equity": _revalue_equity(ledger, ticker, price),
         "cash": ledger.cash,
     }

+"""Focused provenance write/check tests for the live evaluation boundary.
+
+No provider is called. The model boundary is replaced with a recording fake and
+the source fingerprint is monkeypatched so these tests exercise the actual
+provenance ordering and stale-source refusal logic.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+
+from research_desk.eval import live
+from research_desk.eval.live import (
+    PROVENANCE_FILENAME,
+    _provenance_payload,
+    _read_source_fingerprint,
+)
+
+
+def _write(path: Path, data) -> None:
+    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    path.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
+
+
+def _cfg() -> dict:
+    return {
+        "llm_provider": live.PROVIDER,
+        "quick_think_llm": live.MODEL,
+        "deep_think_llm": live.MODEL,
+        "max_tokens": live.OUTPUT_CAP,
+        "temperature": 0,
+    }
+
+
+def test_provenance_payload_uses_actual_model_provider_endpoint_and_config():
+    payload = _provenance_payload(
+        "sha256:abc", _cfg(), "https://example.invalid/v1"
+    )
+
+    assert PROVENANCE_FILENAME == "provenance.json"
+    assert payload["source_fingerprint"] == "sha256:abc"
+    assert payload["model"] == live.MODEL
+    assert payload["provider"] == live.PROVIDER
+    assert payload["endpoint"] == "https://example.invalid/v1"
+    assert payload["deep_think_llm"] == live.MODEL
+    assert payload["max_tokens"] == live.OUTPUT_CAP
+    assert payload["temperature"] == 0
+
+
+def test_read_source_fingerprint_handles_missing_and_invalid(tmp_path):
+    path = tmp_path / PROVENANCE_FILENAME
+    assert _read_source_fingerprint(path) is None
+    _write(path, {"source_fingerprint": "sha256:current"})
+    assert _read_source_fingerprint(path) == "sha256:current"
+    path.write_text("not json", encoding="utf-8")
+    assert _read_source_fingerprint(path) is None
+
+
+class _FakeResult:
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.pack_path = None

+        self.signal = "Hold"
+        self.stop_reason = "completed"
+        self.usage = SimpleNamespace(
+            calls=0, input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, total_tokens=0
+        )
+        self.error = None
+
+
+def _install_fake_runner(monkeypatch, out: Path, seen: list):
+    class _FakeRunner:
+        def __init__(self, settings, **kwargs):
+            self.settings = settings
+            self.context_mode = kwargs.get("context_mode", "baseline")
+
+        def run(self, ticker, trade_date):
+            provenance_path = (
+                Path(out) / ticker.upper() / self.context_mode / PROVENANCE_FILENAME
+            )
+            seen.append(json.loads(provenance_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
+            return _FakeResult()
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr("research_desk.graph_adapter.ResearchRunner", _FakeRunner)
+

+    out = tmp_path / "out"

+        "max_tokens": live.OUTPUT_CAP,

+
+

+    monkeypatch.setattr(live, "_current_source_fingerprint", lambda root: next(fingerprints))
+
+    pack = SimpleNamespace(
+        manifest=SimpleNamespace(outcome="completed"),
+        final_state={"final_trade_decision": "decision"},
+        input=SimpleNamespace(available_sources={}),
+        events=[],
+    )
+    from research_desk.evidence import EvidencePackIO

+    monkeypatch.setattr(EvidencePackIO, "import_pack", lambda self, source: pack)

+    out = tmp_path / "out"

+    _write(
+        out / "AAPL" / "baseline" / PROVENANCE_FILENAME,
+        {"source_fingerprint": "sha256:current"},
+    )
+    judge_prov = out / "judge" / "AAPL" / "baseline" / PROVENANCE_FILENAME

+    def _fake_judge(*args, **kwargs):

+        saved = json.loads(judge_prov.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

+    monkeypatch.setattr(live, "_llm_judge", _fake_judge)
+
+    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="refusing to certify judge results"):
+        live.run_judge_case("AAPL", out)

1: # ADR-004: Bound context and gate release quality
2: 
3: Status: accepted by leo. Scope: the user-authorized project completion revision.
4: 
5: ## Drivers and decision
6: 
7: The final review found a rejected proposal could be reopened by an execution attempt, a missing legal company name, an incorrect quarterly-EPS valuation interpretation, and quality evidence disconnected from merge checks. This revision preserves the original graph and fixed corpus while closing these contracts.
8: 
9: Rejected proposals remain rejected after execution attempts. Review-required recovery applies to pending or previously approved proposals whose terms or current portfolio need another review. The CLI never silently reopens a rejection.
10: 
11: Every model request receives a finite input budget with an earlier compaction threshold. Context assembly retains system constraints, current task, factual evidence and complete assistant/tool groups. It removes or compacts older expendable prose first. If required material still exceeds the cap, the run stops before a provider request and cannot produce an approvable proposal. A conservative UTF-8 byte-based token upper bound may enforce the cap without adding an unpinned model tokenizer; provider usage remains the source for measured cost.
12: 
13: The research output includes a deterministic identity/date/evidence-price section. It renders actual frozen data and complements the generated reasoning. 1: """Proposal review state machine and simulated-ledger execution.
2: 
3: Flow: research produces a PENDING_REVIEW proposal. A trusted CLI operator
4: approves or rejects it. Execution re-evaluates the *current* ledger against the
5: deterministic policy before writing; the approval binds the exact proposal
6: version, so a changed proposal cannot ride an old approval. Re-executing an
7: already-simulated proposal is a no-op (idempotence).
8: 
9: No LLM path reaches this module: the research graph only ever writes a proposal
10: in PENDING_REVIEW, and only the CLI review/execute/ledger commands touch it.
11: """
12: 
13: from __future__ import annotations
14: 
15: import uuid
16: from datetime import datetime, timezone
17: 
18: from .models import (
19:     ExecutionRecord,
20:     ProposalRecord,
21:     ProposalStatus,
22:     TransactionRecord,
23:     TransactionStatus,
24:     make_proposal_version,
25:     utcnow_iso,
26: )
27: from .policy import evaluate_buy, evaluate_sell
28: 
29: # Signals that map to a tradeable buy action; everything else is a sell or
30: # non-tradeable (Hold / REVIEW).
31: BUY_SIGNALS = {"Buy", "Overweight", "Strong Buy"}
32: SELL_SIGNALS = {"Sell", "Underweight", "Reduce"}
33: 
34: 
35: def _side_for_signal(signal: str) -> str:
36:     if signal in BUY_SIGNALS:
37:         return "buy"
38:     if signal in SELL_SIGNALS:
39:         return "sell"
40:     raise ReviewError(f"signal {signal!r} is not tradeable in v1 (Hold/REVIEW do not trade)")
41: 
42: 
43: class ReviewError(Exception):
44:     """Business rejection with a stable message; the ledger stays unchanged."""
45: 
46: 
47: def _proposal_content_version(proposal: ProposalRecord) -> str:
48:     """Fingerprint of the proposal's tradeable inputs, independent of status."""
49:     return make_proposal_version(
50:         proposal.ticker,
51:         proposal.trade_date,
52:         proposal.signal,
53:         proposal.price,
54:         side=proposal.side,
55:         shares=proposal.shares,
56:         evidence_id=proposal.evidence_id,
57:     )
58: 
59: 
60: def create_proposal(
61:     *,
62:     run_id: str,
63:     ticker: str,
64:     trade_date: str,
65:     signal: str,
66:     rating: str | None,
67:     price: float | None,
68:     proposal_id: str | None = None,
69:     evidence_id: str | None = None,
70: ) -> ProposalRecord:
71:     """Create a PENDING_REVIEW proposal from a completed research run.
72: 
73:     Only tradeable signals become proposals: Buy-family signals are buys, Sell-
74:     family signals are sells (up to owned shares, enforced at execution). Hold
75:     and REVIEW never produce a tradeable recommendation.
76:     """
77:     if signal in ("Hold", "REVIEW"):
78:         raise ReviewError(
79:             f"signal {signal!r} is not tradeable in v1; no proposal is created "
80:             "(REVIEW and Hold do not trade)"
81:         )
82:     side = _side_for_signal(signal)
83:     pid = proposal_id or f"prop-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
84:     return ProposalRecord(
85:         proposal_id=pid,
86:         run_id=run_id,
87:         ticker=ticker,
88:         trade_date=trade_date,
89:         signal=signal,
90:         rating=rating,
91:         side=side,
92:         price=price,
93:         evidence_id=evidence_id,
94:         status=ProposalStatus.PENDING_REVIEW,
95:         proposal_version=_proposal_content_version(
96:             ProposalRecord(
97:                 proposal_id=pid,
98:                 run_id=run_id,
99:                 ticker=ticker,
100:                 trade_date=trade_date,
101:                 signal=signal,
102:                 rating=rating,
103:                 side=side,
104:                 price=price,
105:                 evidence_id=evidence_id,
106:             )
107:         ),
108:         created_at=utcnow_iso(),
109:     )
110: 
111: 
112: def approve(
113:     proposal: ProposalRecord,
114:     *,
115:     shares: int,
116:     operator: str,
117: ) -> ProposalRecord:
118:     """Approve an exact proposal version with an operator-supplied share count.
119: 
120:     The approval is bound to the proposal's *content* version, so if the run's
121:     material inputs (ticker/date/signal/price) later change, the old approval
122:     no longer matches and execution requires review.
123:     """
124:     if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
125:         raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated")
126:     if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED:
127:         raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is rejected and cannot be approved")
128:     # REVIEW_REQUIRED is a safe-fail state, not a dead end: after the operator
129:     # reviews the current evidence, they may approve the corrected version.
130:     if not operator:
131:         raise ReviewError("approval requires an operator identity")
132:     if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:
133:         raise ReviewError(f"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}")
134:     if proposal.price is None or proposal.price <= 0:
135:         raise ReviewError(
136:             f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} has no evidence price; cannot approve without price"
137:         )
138:     proposal.shares = shares
139:     proposal.operator = operator
140:     proposal.status = ProposalStatus.APPROVED
141:     proposal.approved_at = utcnow_iso()
142:     proposal.approved_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)
143:     return proposal
144: 
145: 
146: def reject(proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str, reason: str = "rejected by operator") -> ProposalRecord:
147:     if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
148:         raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated")
149:     proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REJECTED
150:     proposal.operator = operator
151:     proposal.reason = reason
152:     return proposal
153: 
154: 
155: def execute(
156:     store, proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str,
157: ) -> tuple[ProposalRecord, ExecutionRecord]:
158:     """Re-evaluate the current ledger and simulate the approved buy (or reject).
159: 
160:     Steps (each observable, none partial):
161:     1. Idempotence: an already-SIMULATED proposal returns its stored execution.
162:     2. Version binding: the current proposal content must match the approved
163:        version; otherwise REVIEW_REQUIRED (AT-05).
164:     3. Re-read the current ledger and run the deterministic policy.
165:     4. On any failure: return REVIEW_REQUIRED / BLOCKED with reasons; ledger
166:        unchanged. On success: apply the transaction atomically.
167:     """
168:     if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
169:         existing = proposal.execution or ExecutionRecord(executed=True)
170:         existing.reason = "already executed"
171:         return proposal, existing
172: 
173:     current_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)
174:     # A stale approval for different content is checked before status: an
175:     # approved proposal whose run inputs changed must not execute the new
176:     # version (AT-05), even though the row now carries the new content.
177:     if proposal.approved_version is not None and proposal.approved_version != current_version:
178:         proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
179:         proposal.reason = (
180:             "approval no longer matches the proposal content (version changed "
181:             f"approved={proposal.approved_version!r} current={current_version!r}); "
182:             "re-review against the current ledger"
183:         )
184:         store.update_proposal_status(
185:             proposal.proposal_id,
186:             ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED,
187:             operator=operator,
188:             reason=proposal.reason,
189:         )
190:         return proposal, ExecutionRecord(
191:             executed=False, reason=proposal.reason, policy_checks=[]
192:         )
193:     if proposal.status != ProposalStatus.APPROVED:
194:         proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
195:         proposal.reason = (
196:             f"proposal is not APPROVED (status={proposal.status.value}) and cannot "
197:             "execute; approve it against the current ledger first"
198:         )
199:         store.update_proposal_status(
200:             proposal.proposal_id,
201:             ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED,
202:             operator=operator,
203:             reason=proposal.reason,
204:         )

in PENDING_REVIEW, and only the CLI review/execute/ledger commands touch it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from .models import (
    ExecutionRecord,
    ProposalRecord,
    ProposalStatus,
    TransactionRecord,
    TransactionStatus,
    make_proposal_version,
    utcnow_iso,
)
from .policy import evaluate_buy, evaluate_sell

# Signals that map to a tradeable buy action; everything else is a sell or
# non-tradeable (Hold / REVIEW).
BUY_SIGNALS = {"Buy", "Overweight", "Strong Buy"}
SELL_SIGNALS = {"Sell", "Underweight", "Reduce"}


def _side_for_signal(signal: str) -> str:
    if signal in BUY_SIGNALS:
        return "buy"
    if signal in SELL_SIGNALS:
        return "sell"
    raise ReviewError(f"signal {signal!r} is not tradeable in v1 (Hold/REVIEW do not trade)")


class ReviewError(Exception):
    """Business rejection with a stable message; the ledger stays unchanged."""


def _proposal_content_version(proposal: ProposalRecord) -> str:
    """Fingerprint of the proposal's tradeable inputs, independent of status."""
    return make_proposal_version(
        proposal.ticker,
        proposal.trade_date,
        proposal.signal,
        proposal.price,
        side=proposal.side,
        shares=proposal.shares,
        evidence_id=proposal.evidence_id,
    )


def create_proposal(
    *,
    run_id: str,
    ticker: str,
    trade_date: str,
    signal: str,
    rating: str | None,
    price: float | None,
    proposal_id: str | None = None,
    evidence_id: str | None = None,
) -> ProposalRecord:
    """Create a PENDING_REVIEW proposal from a completed research run.

    Only tradeable signals become proposals: Buy-family signals are buys, Sell-
    family signals are sells (up to owned shares, enforced at execution). Hold
    and REVIEW never produce a tradeable recommendation.
    """
    if signal in ("Hold", "REVIEW"):
        raise ReviewError(
            f"signal {signal!r} is not tradeable in v1; no proposal is created "
            "(REVIEW and Hold do not trade)"
        )
    side = _side_for_signal(signal)
    pid = proposal_id or f"prop-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    return ProposalRecord(
        proposal_id=pid,
        run_id=run_id,
        ticker=ticker,
        trade_date=trade_date,
        signal=signal,
        rating=rating,
        side=side,
        price=price,
        evidence_id=evidence_id,
        status=ProposalStatus.PENDING_REVIEW,
        proposal_version=_proposal_content_version(
            ProposalRecord(
                proposal_id=pid,
                run_id=run_id,
                ticker=ticker,
                trade_date=trade_date,
                signal=signal,
                rating=rating,
                side=side,
                price=price,
                evidence_id=evidence_id,
            )
        ),
        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
    )


def approve(
    proposal: ProposalRecord,
    *,
    shares: int,
    operator: str,
) -> ProposalRecord:
    """Approve an exact proposal version with an operator-supplied share count.

    The approval is bound to the proposal's *content* version, so if the run's
    material inputs (ticker/date/signal/price) later change, the old approval
    no longer matches and execution requires review.
    """
    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
        raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated")
    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.REJECTED:
        raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is rejected and cannot be approved")
    # REVIEW_REQUIRED is a safe-fail state, not a dead end: after the operator
    # reviews the current evidence, they may approve the corrected version.
    if not operator:
        raise ReviewError("approval requires an operator identity")
    if not isinstance(shares, int) or shares <= 0:
        raise ReviewError(f"shares must be a positive integer, got {shares!r}")
    if proposal.price is None or proposal.price <= 0:
        raise ReviewError(
            f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} has no evidence price; cannot approve without price"
        )
    proposal.shares = shares
    proposal.operator = operator
    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.APPROVED
    proposal.approved_at = utcnow_iso()
    proposal.approved_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)
    return proposal


def reject(proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str, reason: str = "rejected by operator") -> ProposalRecord:
    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
        raise ReviewError(f"proposal {proposal.proposal_id} is already simulated")
    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REJECTED
    proposal.operator = operator
    proposal.reason = reason
    return proposal


def execute(
    store, proposal: ProposalRecord, *, operator: str,
) -> tuple[ProposalRecord, ExecutionRecord]:
    """Re-evaluate the current ledger and simulate the approved buy (or reject).

    Steps (each observable, none partial):
    1. Idempotence: an already-SIMULATED proposal returns its stored execution.
    2. Version binding: the current proposal content must match the approved
       version; otherwise REVIEW_REQUIRED (AT-05).
    3. Re-read the current ledger and run the deterministic policy.
    4. On any failure: return REVIEW_REQUIRED / BLOCKED with reasons; ledger
       unchanged. On success: apply the transaction atomically.
    """
    if proposal.status == ProposalStatus.SIMULATED:
        existing = proposal.execution or ExecutionRecord(executed=True)
        existing.reason = "already executed"
        return proposal, existing

    current_version = _proposal_content_version(proposal)
    # A stale approval for different content is checked before status: an
    # approved proposal whose run inputs changed must not execute the new
    # version (AT-05), even though the row now carries the new content.
    if proposal.approved_version is not None and proposal.approved_version != current_version:
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = (
            "approval no longer matches the proposal content (version changed "
            f"approved={proposal.approved_version!r} current={current_version!r}); "
            "re-review against the current ledger"
        )
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id,
            ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED,
            operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(
            executed=False, reason=proposal.reason, policy_checks=[]
        )
    if proposal.status != ProposalStatus.APPROVED:
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = (
            f"proposal is not APPROVED (status={proposal.status.value}) and cannot "
            "execute; approve it against the current ledger first"
        )
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id,
            ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED,
            operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(
            executed=False, reason=proposal.reason, policy_checks=[]
        )

    if proposal.shares is None or proposal.price is None:
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = "proposal missing shares or evidence price; cannot execute"
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id, ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED, operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(executed=False, reason=proposal.reason, policy_checks=[])

    ledger = store.get_ledger()
    if ledger is None:
        raise ReviewError("ledger is not initialised")

    if proposal.side == "sell":
        return _execute_sell(store, proposal, ledger, operator=operator)
    verdict = evaluate_buy(ledger, proposal.ticker, proposal.shares, proposal.price)
    if not verdict.allowed:
        reasons = [f"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}" for c in verdict.checks if not c["passed"]]
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = "policy failed at execution time: " + "; ".join(reasons)
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id, ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED, operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(
            executed=False,
            reason=proposal.reason,
            policy_checks=verdict.checks,
            equity_before=ledger.equity,
        )

    tx_id = f"tx-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    execution = ExecutionRecord(
        executed=True,
        tx_id=tx_id,
        policy_checks=verdict.checks,
        equity_before=ledger.equity,
        equity_after=ledger.equity,
        cash_delta=-proposal.shares * proposal.price,
    )
    tx = TransactionRecord(
        tx_id=tx_id,
        proposal_id=proposal.proposal_id,
        ticker=proposal.ticker,
        side="buy",
        shares=proposal.shares,
        price=proposal.price,
        cash_delta=execution.cash_delta,
        equity_before=ledger.equity,
        equity_after=ledger.equity,
        status=TransactionStatus.SIMULATED,
        policy_checks=verdict.checks,
        operator=operator,
        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
    )
    store.apply_transaction(tx, execution)
    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.SIMULATED
    proposal.execution = execution
    updated = store.get_proposal(proposal.proposal_id)
    return updated or proposal, proposal.execution


def _execute_sell(store, proposal: ProposalRecord, ledger, *, operator: str):
    """Execute an approved sell up to owned shares; apply the transaction atomically."""
    shares = proposal.shares
    price = proposal.price
    if shares is None or price is None:
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = "proposal missing shares or evidence price; cannot execute"
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id, ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED, operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(executed=False, reason=proposal.reason, policy_checks=[])

    verdict = evaluate_sell(ledger, proposal.ticker, shares, price)
    if not verdict.allowed:
        reasons = [f"{c['check']}: {c['detail']}" for c in verdict.checks if not c["passed"]]
        proposal.status = ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED
        proposal.reason = "policy failed at execution time: " + "; ".join(reasons)
        store.update_proposal_status(
            proposal.proposal_id, ProposalStatus.REVIEW_REQUIRED, operator=operator,
            reason=proposal.reason,
        )
        return proposal, ExecutionRecord(
            executed=False,
            reason=proposal.reason,
            policy_checks=verdict.checks,
            equity_before=ledger.equity,
        )

    tx_id = f"tx-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
    execution = ExecutionRecord(
        executed=True,
        tx_id=tx_id,
        policy_checks=verdict.checks,
        equity_before=ledger.equity,
        equity_after=ledger.equity,
        cash_delta=shares * price,
    )
    tx = TransactionRecord(
        tx_id=tx_id,
        proposal_id=proposal.proposal_id,
        ticker=proposal.ticker,
        side="sell",
        shares=shares,
        price=price,
        cash_delta=execution.cash_delta,
        equity_before=ledger.equity,
        equity_after=ledger.equity,
        status=TransactionStatus.SIMULATED,
        policy_checks=verdict.checks,
        operator=operator,
        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
    )
    store.apply_transaction(tx, execution)
    proposal.status = ProposalStatus.SIMULATED
    proposal.execution = execution
    updated = store.get_proposal(proposal.proposal_id)
    return updated or proposal, proposal.execution


def evaluate_proposal_legibility(proposal: ProposalRecord) -> list[str]:
    """Non-mutating advisory checks used by the CLI ledger/report views."""
    issues: list[str] = []
